subject: Urgent: Brightleaf production latency spike — cross-region evacuation plan
messages:
From: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@brightleaf.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightleaf Ops <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency and 5xx surge in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Olga —

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency and 5xx errors hitting our production workspace in us-west-2 at ~07:50 PT. Key observations: p95 latency spiked to ~1.2s (baseline ~180ms), overall success rate dropped to ~92% with a lot of downstream 502/504s. Traffic is normal for the hour, nothing on our side that explains a surge.

This is impacting our user flows (search & upload). Can you confirm whether this is a regional infra issue on Redwood's side and if you can initiate cross-region routing / failover to eu-west-1 while you investigate? We need an ETA for mitigation.

I've attached a small set of traces and a flamegraph from our client side.

Attachments: trace_samples_20270914.json

Thanks,
Alex
Account Director — Brightleaf AI
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@brightleaf.ai>, Brightleaf Ops <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx surge in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Alex — thanks for the signal and the traces. We're seeing elevated queuing and a rise in tail latency on our us-west-2 AZs correlated with a degraded disk throughput on a shard of the serving tier.

Immediate actions I'm authorizing now (executing in parallel):
- Rishi: please start the traffic evacuation runbook (playbook_evacuate_v1.pdf) and open an incident in the console.
- Marissa: notify Brightleaf PD and provide an ETA message for customers; please coordinate exec escalation if they request credits.
- Stephanie: warm eu-west-1 (model variants and KV caches) and prepare a 5% canary shift.

Alex — we'll propose a staged cross-region steer: canary 5% -> 30% -> 100% if metrics look good. Expect first shift within 20 minutes. We'll confirm each step.

Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

---
Attachments: playbook_evacuate_v1.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx surge in us-west-2 — immediate help requested

Team — quick technical plan and constraints: 
1) Root cause indicators: one of the NVMe rings in us-west-2 serving tier shows I/O stalls; pod-level CPU looks normal but read latency elevated. We can't rely on partial AZ fixes without risking flapping.
2) Failover plan: shift traffic at the API gateway layer by updating routing policy for Brightleaf's org ID. Steps: 5% -> 30% -> 100% (10-min observation windows).
3) Compatibility: eu-west-1 has the same model family but uses a 16-bit quantized variant; quality delta expected to be negligible for search use-cases. KV cache warming should be handled by a t=0 pre-warm job I will kick off.
4) Metrics to watch: 95th latency, 5xx rate, token throughput, request fanout. I will hook a temporary dashboard and share link.

I'll start the routing change now and post updates here.

Rishi
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: runbook_step_log.txt (posted to incident)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Status update — initiating cross-region canary (Brightleaf)

Alex — FYI we're initiating a 5% canary to eu-west-1 now per Olga/Rishi's plan. Rishi has kicked the KV warmers and the routing change is live for canary traffic. We'll validate for two 10-minute windows and then escalate to 30% if steady.

Markus — looping you in for exec awareness. Brightleaf may request an SLA exception or credits depending on impact; please advise on authorization band for immediate customer remedies.

Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@brightleaf.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightleaf Ops <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Status update — initiating cross-region canary (Brightleaf)

Thanks — please proceed with the ramp to 30% if the first window looks stable. If you have an ETA for full cutover, share it and we'll broadcast to our internal on-call. We are authorizing the shift.

— Alex
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@brightleaf.ai>, Brightleaf Ops <ops@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency and 5xx surge in us-west-2 — cross-region evacuation complete

Alex — final update: we completed the staged evacuation to eu-west-1. Timeline: 08:40 canary 5% -> 09:00 ramped to 30% -> 09:30 reached 100% traffic to eu-west-1 after 10-minute steady windows. Post-evac metrics: p95 back near baseline (~220ms), 5xx stabilized <0.5%. We continue to monitor and will keep Brightleaf on the incident page.

Next steps:
- We will keep a small canary footprint in us-west-2 for 24h and perform rolling replacement of the degraded NVMe nodes.
- Rishi will produce a postmortem with timeline and root cause within 72h.
- Markus will follow up on any credit/SLA remediation discussions with your finance team.

Apologies for the disruption — thanks for the quick coordination.

Olga Petrov
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
